course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Global Conflict
unit.description: Study how empires collapsed, why two world wars were fought and how they were conducted, how the Depression reshaped economies, and how mass atrocities happened.

stimulusBlocks.attribution: John Maynard Keynes, British economist and Treasury representative at the Paris Peace Conference who resigned in protest in June 1919, The Economic Consequences of the Peace, 1919
stimulusBlocks.citation: John Maynard Keynes, The Economic Consequences of the Peace (New York: Harcourt, Brace and Howe, 1920), chs. 6–7. Project Gutenberg eBook #15776.
stimulusBlocks.note: The Central Empires were Germany and Austria-Hungary. “The late German war” is the First World War.
stimulusBlocks.text:
This chapter must be one of pessimism. The Treaty includes no provisions for the economic rehabilitation of Europe,--nothing to make the defeated Central Empires into good neighbors, nothing to stabilize the new States of Europe, nothing to reclaim Russia . . . .

If we aim deliberately at the impoverishment of Central Europe, vengeance, I dare predict, will not limp. Nothing can then delay for very long that final civil war between the forces of Reaction and the despairing convulsions of Revolution, before which the horrors of the late German war will fade into nothing . . . .

questions.prompt: According to the passage, mandates were territories
choices: returned to the Ottoman Empire
governed by the United States
supervised by victors until judged ready for independence

choiceExplanations: Victors supervised them under the League of Nations.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.5 key concept: after World War I, the mandate system and the Paris peace settlement left unresolved tensions, especially in the former Ottoman territories
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the mandate system after World War I
stimulusBlocks.text:
The peace settlement after World War I gave Germany's colonies and the Ottoman Empire's Arab lands to the victors as mandates, territories to be supervised under the League of Nations until they were judged ready for independence. France received Syria and Lebanon, and Britain received Iraq, Palestine, and Transjordan.

Many Arabs had fought against the Ottomans expecting independence. To them, the mandates looked like colonialism under a new name. In Palestine, Britain had also promised support for a Jewish national home, which set the stage for lasting conflict.

questions.prompt: Many Arabs viewed the mandates as colonialism under a new name because

they had fought the Ottomans expecting independence
the mandates were ruled by Arab kings
the mandates were given to Japan
questions.explanation: They expected independence but received British and French control.
choiceExplanations: They expected independence but received British and French control.
Japan received only Pacific islands, not Arab lands.
questions.distinguisher: Many Arabs fought against the Ottomans, not for them.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.5 key concept: nationalist and anticolonial movements grew after World War I, as in India and China
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing anticolonial movements after World War I
stimulusBlocks.text:
On May 4, 1919, students in Beijing protested the decision at Paris to give Germany's rights in China's Shandong province to Japan. The May Fourth Movement spread across China and called for national strength and modern reforms.

In India, Mohandas Gandhi led campaigns of nonviolent noncooperation against British rule. In 1930 he led the Salt March to protest the British tax on salt. These movements drew millions of ordinary people into politics.

questions.prompt: Which concern does Keynes express about the peace settlement in the passage?
choices: It treated Germany too leniently and left it strong enough to threaten Europe
It gave too much territory to Russia and its new government
It offered no plan for Europe's recovery and risked provoking revolution
It left the League of Nations without any power to enforce its decisions
questions.explanation: Keynes says the treaty had no provisions for rehabilitating Europe and warns of civil war and revolution if Central Europe is impoverished.
choiceExplanations: Keynes argues the settlement was too harsh, not too lenient.
The passage says the treaty did nothing to reclaim Russia, not that it enlarged it.
Keynes says the treaty had no provisions for rehabilitating Europe and warns of civil war and revolution if Central Europe is impoverished.
The passage does not discuss the League of Nations.
questions.distinguisher: Germany was disarmed under the treaty, but Keynes's concern is economic ruin, not military limits.

choices: He was a German official appointed to defend Germany at Paris
He was a soldier who sought revenge for the war's destruction

questions.explanation: Keynes advised the British Treasury at Paris and left in June 1919 because he thought the settlement would harm Europe.
choiceExplanations: Keynes was British and represented the British Treasury.
Keynes was an economist, not a soldier.
The League of Nations had not yet been established when he resigned.
Keynes advised the British Treasury at Paris and left in June 1919 because he thought the settlement would harm Europe.

questions.prompt: Which events of the 1920s and 1930s most clearly support Keynes's prediction?
choices: Lasting prosperity in Germany and steady payment of reparations after 1919
Economic crisis in Germany and the rise of extremists such as the Nazi Party
The Russian Revolution of 1917 and the fall of the tsar
The creation of the mandate system in the Middle East
questions.explanation: Hyperinflation in 1923 and the Great Depression helped the Nazis gain support, as Keynes had warned that economic ruin could breed extremism.
choiceExplanations: Keynes predicted trouble, and Germany instead suffered inflation and depression.
Hyperinflation in 1923 and the Great Depression helped the Nazis gain support, as Keynes had warned that economic ruin could breed extremism.
The Russian Revolution took place two years before Keynes wrote, so it cannot confirm his prediction.
The mandates governed former Ottoman and German colonial lands and do not bear on Keynes's warning.
questions.distinguisher: Revolution had already occurred in Russia, but Keynes was predicting what would follow the treaty.
